newsitem.title: INDIA: India ONGC hopeful of deep-sea crude.
newsitem.headline: India ONGC hopeful of deep-sea crude.

text.p: India's Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) is hopeful of a large crude oil discovery in deep sea areas of the Kerala-Konkan basin on its west coast, its chairman said.

"Seismic surveys of areas in the deep sea indicate large structures as big as Bombay High, especially in the Kerala-Konkan area. This is not so in the case of the Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery basins where hydrocarbon reserves will be smaller," B.C. Bora told Reuters in an interview late on Thursday.
The ONGC has been allocated the three deep-sea blocks on a nomination basis. The government will be inviting bids for other deep-sea blocks towards the end of the year, Bora said.
"Deep-water areas off the east coast of Andaman islands have also been evaluated by the Director General of Hydrocarbons to hold large structure of natural gas," Bora said.

He said Marubeni Corp of Japan, in association with Brazilian firm Petroleo Brasileiro SA (Petrobras), has shown keen interest in joining hands with ONGC for deep-sea exploration. "Broadly they have shown interest in Kerala-Konkan, Cauvery and Krishna-Godavari basins."
"We are also trying to work out areas in which we should go alone and areas where we should have partners to share the risk as well as provide technology," Bora said.
